question: Which type of placentation is characterized by the ovules developing on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part, as seen in mustard and argemone?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Parietal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Parietal placentation occurs when the ovules are attached to the inner walls of the ovary or on its peripheral part.
 
• This type of placentation is commonly observed in plants like **mustard** (Brassica) and **argemone**.
 
• The ovary in parietal placentation is typically unilocular but may become bilocular or multilocular due to the development of a false septum.
 
• In this arrangement, the ovules are borne on the ovary walls rather than on a central column.
 
• Parietal placentation is distinct from other types such as axile, basal, or free central, each of which has a unique ovule arrangement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Placentation**: It refers to the arrangement of ovules within the ovary. It plays a key role in plant reproduction and is an important taxonomic characteristic.
 
• **Axile placentation**: The ovules are attached to a central axis in a multilocular ovary, as seen in plants like tomato and lemon.
 
• **Basal placentation**: The ovules are borne at the base of the ovary, as in marigold and sunflower.
 
• **Free central placentation**: The ovules are attached to a central column, and the ovary is unilocular, as seen in dianthus.
 
• Understanding placentation types helps in the identification and classification of flowering plants, contributing to botany and plant systematics.
